summary: Diagnostic remediation intent DSL and todo2code analysis

delivery.outcome: Target repositories can turn stable diagnostics into validated, hash-bound remediation intents that an LLM and todo2code can analyze without expanding approved scope or authority
nonGoals: No Diagit implementation, ticket, task log or release artifact is stored in the governance hub
No LLM or todo2code output becomes a deterministic merge decision
No automatic cleanup of dirty worktrees or unreadable paths
No v0.15.0 publication or ticket-065 closure

architecture.decision: Keep reusable code/runbook remediation separate from one target ticket's JSON DSL; validate and render deterministically, then bind todo2code advisory findings to the intent projection digest
interfaceChanges: hash-bound advisoryAnalysis projection in the DSL
adopted .governance remediation schema, template and analyzer
dataChanges: Target ticket may contain remediation-intent.dsl.json with facts, applicability, ordered steps, verification and advisory analysis
architecture.rollback: Revert the unmerged ticket branch; adopted targets remain pinned to their previous immutable standard revision

validation.evidence: Positive and negative DSL fixtures exercise structure, graph, applicability, safety and verification semantics

commands: python3 scripts/remediation_intent.py analyze-todo2code fixture --diagnostics diagnostics.json --plans code-change-plans.json
validation.evidence: Stable projections and advisory overlay are digest-bound and detect plan scope/criterion mismatches
Sanitized Diagit-shaped fixture preserves blockers, dependencies and dirty-worktree non-automation

commands: all commands from the Linux CI test job
deterministic todo2code pipeline against rendered task
validation.evidence: Hub contracts and real todo2code output remain consistent without runtime dependency additions
